name: 9559-batchdecode-235ba22bfp8-tp4
model: Qwen/Qwen3-235B-A22B-FP8. Not substitutable: the topology below follows from its FP8 block quantization (weight_block_size [128, 128]) and its 128 routed experts at moe_intermediate_size 1536.
hardware: 4x H100 80GB HBM3, one node, no router and no cache tier outside it.
parallelism: TP=4, EP=1, PP=1, DP=1. Forced: moe_intermediate_size 1536 must stay divisible by the FP8 block width 128 after sharding, so TP8 (192) will not start and TP2 needs ~111 GiB per card.
load_profile: concurrent (closed loop), streams=32, warmup the first 20%, bounded at 320 requests with a 2400 s safety cap; ~256 requests measured.
workload: guidellm synthetic_text, single turn, no prefix reuse and the engine's prefix cache disabled: 128 prompt tokens in and 512 output tokens out, both fixed, with temperature 0.0 and ignore_eos true.
purpose: A long-form answer generator on a 235-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model, serving 32 concurrent short prompts on four GPUs.
launch:
# ENGINE: sglang at commit a0b22f2f170be9d61cc3335b36af3bfb9ed709ce
#   (`git describe --tags --match 'v*'` = v0.5.1.post1-6-ga0b22f2f170). A commit rather than a
#   release, so the interpreter is named by `configs/env.yaml: venv`.
model-path: Qwen/Qwen3-235B-A22B-FP8

# FORCED, not chosen: moe_intermediate_size 1536 / TP must stay divisible by the FP8 block width
# 128. TP4 gives 384 and runs; TP8 gives 192 and the server refuses to start.
tp-size: 4

# DO NOT LOWER BELOW 32, the declared stream count: below it decode steps fall off the captured
# graphs onto the eager path and the run measures the engine's Python instead.
cuda-graph-max-bs: 64

disable-radix-cache: true

# host / port / served-model-name are owned by whatever starts the server. Everything else --
# chunked-prefill-size, mem-fraction-static, context-length, attention-backend, dtype,
# quantization, ep-size, max-running-requests -- is left at the stock value of this commit.
